task: EPMCDME-15401: add a bridge channel (injected stdlib-only SDK, side thread with own exec calls, per-run exchange folder, echo handler) so a script on a pooled sandbox pod can call the backend during a run, with env-wide switch, 120 s tool-calling limit, timeout process kill, folder cleanup/sweep and import-allowlist tests.

key_reasoning.reason: Four or more components in one repo with a new abstraction: WorkspaceScriptRunner, CodeExecutorTool._execute_code_sandbox (per-pod lock, timeout), sandbox_guard wrapper builder (SDK injection), CodeExecutorConfig (switch and limit), new SDK/constants folder, new side-channel and exchange-folder helper, plus a per-run opt-in carrier through AgentWorkspaceService.

Closest pattern is the manual minikube spike plus the guard-wrapper subprocess tests; there is no production precedent for a concurrent side channel over separate k8s exec calls. Unverified: stopping the script's process in a shared pod without hitting other conversations, running the injected SDK under the audit-hook guard, 120 s runs against the 300 s session TTL and the per-pod lock. Security-sensitive: the existing guard does not cover exchange-data isolation, so this gap is a divergence and adds to the score, and sandbox enforcement must not be weakened. Enumerated edge cases (size cap, concurrent runs, timeout, interruption) have no existing defensive test template (no import-allowlist, clean-interpreter or k8s exec fake). Held at XL because the spike reduces true novelty.

About 5-7 modified files (runner, code_executor_tool, sandbox_guard, models, README, agent_workspace_service, possibly toolkit) and 3-5 new source files (SDK, constants, channel/exchange helper, cleanup) plus 4-6 new test files, across src/codemie_tools and src/codemie and tests: new-file count lands in XL.
